question.problem:
Find the orthogonal projection of the vector $x$ onto the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ 4\end{aligned}].
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $v$ and $w$ are linearly independent. 

The orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ spanned by the columns of a matrix $A$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x=A({A}^{T}\,A)^{-1}\,{A}^{T}\,x.
$$

Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}\{v,w\}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ In our case, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}| & | \\ v & w \\ | & |\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,{A}^{T}=[\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, we get the following projection:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {([\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}])}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 & -2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}4 \\ -6 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot {[\begin{aligned}17 & -1 \\ -1 & 3\end{aligned}]}^{-1}\cdot [\begin{aligned}16 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot \frac{1}{50}[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 17\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}16 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
